title: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine, US and Russia Plan November Peace Talks
excerpt: According to Times Now, Zelenskyy says three-way talks are planned for November. The proposed meeting would test whether renewed diplomacy can produce practical progress.
author: LokkeeVerse
content:
Ukraine, the United States and Russia are expected to hold three-way peace talks in November, according to Times Now, which reports that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the planned meeting. The report says Moscow has agreed in principle to resume negotiations after November 10, following US envoy Steve Witkoff’s meetings with both sides. The initiative would seek to restart stalled diplomacy over Russia’s war in Ukraine, although an agreement to meet is not the same as agreement on a settlement.

## What Three-Way Talks Could Change

A trilateral format would bring Ukraine, Russia and a major diplomatic actor into the same negotiating process. Direct participation matters because any durable arrangement would require decisions by the countries fighting the war, alongside clarity about what outside partners could support or help enforce. Washington’s role is significant given its military, economic and diplomatic relationship with Kyiv.

The distinction between an agreement in principle and a confirmed meeting remains important. Diplomatic preparations typically involve settling the venue, participants, agenda and procedures before substantive bargaining begins. The reported November window signals an intention to resume contact, but it does not by itself establish that those practical arrangements have been completed or that the parties share a common starting position.

## The Obstacles to a Lasting Agreement

The central issues extend well beyond scheduling. Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022 intensified a conflict rooted in its 2014 seizure of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine. Territory, Ukrainian sovereignty and future security arrangements remain fundamental concerns. Negotiators would also need to distinguish between steps aimed at reducing immediate violence and commitments intended to prevent another war.

Even a narrower ceasefire would raise difficult implementation questions: how violations would be monitored, who would investigate disputed incidents and what consequences would follow. Humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchanges and protection of civilians, can offer areas for practical diplomacy. Such measures would not resolve the broader conflict, but they could provide concrete tests of whether negotiations are producing results.

- Times Now attributes the planned November talks to Zelenskyy.
- Russia’s reported assent is in principle, rather than a completed peace agreement.
- Participation, security commitments and enforcement would shape the talks’ significance.

Readers should watch for official confirmation from all three governments, a firm meeting date and details of the negotiating agenda. The clearest measure of progress will be specific, verifiable commitments—not simply the announcement that discussions will resume.
